title: Fifth Report: Children Harmed at Alpha School's Boot Camp
author: Benjamin Riley
summary: Benjamin Riley continues his investigative series on Alpha School with a report on its high school boot camp, centered on a three-day outdoor Survival Challenge held September 18 to 20, 2026 at a Texas ranch. Citing multiple sources and a public-records request, he reports that a student fell, was concussed, and received advanced life support before ambulance evacuation, and that local police have confirmed an open investigation. He adds accounts of heat exhaustion, a walk without water, an unscreened shower facility, and cameras and drones trained on sleeping students. Riley documents the ranch's opaque ownership and Alpha School's silence in response to his requests for comment. A comparison from veteran outdoor educator Dylan Kane notes that such unsupervised expeditions come only at the end of a heavily supported program and have been scaled back by outdoor schools because of persistent safety problems. Riley closes with direct commentary to students, parents, staff, founders and the wider education community, and a lighter travel section on Texas barbecue.
points: Riley's central claim is that an AI-forward, low-adult-supervision school model has now produced documented physical harm, with a hospitalization and an active police investigation rather than just pedagogical concerns.
The report ties the incident to design choices, since about 73 teenagers were left largely unsupervised on a 250-acre campground while guides camped a 20 to 30 minute walk away.
Outdoor-education expert Dylan Kane supplies the key contrast: comparable programs place unsupervised stretches at the end of a well-supported sequence and still abandoned them over risk management.
Student privacy emerges as a second failure, with an unscreened shower facility and cameras and drones capturing students overnight, raising the question of who holds the footage.
The piece models how to report on a school whose own communications are silent, using public-records requests, named official contacts and multiple-source confirmation before publishing.
quotes: The good news is that every student appears to have actually survived the Survival Challenge. The less good news is that one student fell and was concussed, and had to be provided advanced life support services on-site before being evacuated by ambulance to the local ER.

In general, during the Survival Challenge, sources report that students were largely left unsupervised for three days. Although adult guides were present at River Rock Ranch, they set up camp separately from the students, approximately 20-30 minutes away by foot.
But leaving approximately 73 teenage students largely unsupervised by adults on a 250-acre campground for multiple days obviously increases the likelihood of such an accident occurring.

My organization, and several other similar outdoor education organizations, scaled back practices like these because we struggled to manage risk and avoid incidents, and because we felt we could get similar learning outcomes with more adult oversight.
So all we know right now is that there is an open and active investigation by Victoria County police related to the Survival Challenge on the River Rock Ranch.
Multiple sources indicated that Go Pro cameras were placed around where students camped, and positioned to face the area where students slept at night. I’m also told drones were omnipresent.
Alpha School is in complete crisis. Children are being harmed. The police are investigating. And the false narrative that its leadership has long presented to the world is destroyed forever.
